summary: The change does solve the task: on the baseline commit the new acceptance test fails with blocking diagnostics for nested/empty/readonly anonymous literals, and with the patch it passes, the whole repo test suite is green, and ~30 hand-written semantic probes (assignments, arguments, returns, nesting, spreads, optional/readonly views, record and union contexts, empty literals) lower, verify, and produce correct Go and ABAP output with no regression I could find versus the baseline. Shape sharing is order-insensitive and readonly/optional views reuse one physical class as required. Two minor observations remain: a pre-existing evaluation-order hazard that the patch only partially mitigates, and an unrelated-looking tweak to LSP call handling.

findings.claim: Object-literal members are evaluated in constructor-parameter order, not source order, whenever a shape class is reused for a literal whose property order differs. The new lower_shape.go mitigation (tempInit when impure > 1, line 450) only covers the rarely-taken anonymousLiteral path and not the impure==1-plus-pure-read case, so the hazard remains in the common path the patch relies on. Identical behavior on the baseline commit, so this is a pre-existing minor bug, not a regression.
findings.repro: Source: `export class Probe { static v = 0; static next(): number { Probe.v++; return Probe.v; } static run(): number { const a = {x: 0, y: 0}; const b = {y: Probe.next(), x: Probe.v}; return b.x * 10 + b.y; } }` — JS semantics give 11 (next() first, then x reads v==1); the lowered program prints 1 (x read v==0 first) both with the patch and on the baseline.

findings.claim: Restricting lspCall to symbols with SymbolFlagsModule is unrelated to the anonymous-shape task and is not exercised by any test: `git checkout baseline -- tsfront/lower_lsp.go && go test ./...` still passes fully with the rest of the patch applied. It looks like a defensible hardening (only declaration-merged namespaces construct LSP values), but as an untested behavior change bundled into this patch it is scope creep a reviewer should be told about.
findings.repro: cd /work && git stash push tsfront/lower_lsp.go >/dev/null 2>&1 || git checkout baseline -- tsfront/lower_lsp.go; go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -3; git checkout HEAD -- tsfront/lower_lsp.go  # suite is green either way
